en: The Apadāna of the Elder Akkamanadāyaka Jagatidāyakavagga, Chapter 5 The Apadāna of the Elder Akkamanadāyaka: In the past, during the time of the Buddha Kassapa, I was a householder in the city of Bandhumatī. At that time, I built a stone terrace for the Sangha; Having offered it with a devoted heart, I passed away from that life. By the power of that merit, I was reborn in heaven, And after enjoying celestial bliss for many eons, I was born here in the world of men as a human being. Because of that deed, my body is now free from disease. Even when I am struck by a great calamity, My body does not suffer pain or affliction. This stone terrace, which I offered in the past, Is the cause of my present well-being. Thus did the Elder Akkamanadāyaka speak of his own past deeds. May all beings be well and happy!
as he was departing for his midday rest...”
I gave the gift of a foot-stool.
that gift which I gave at that time—
I do not know a miserable rebirth;
this is the fruit of my treading [upon the path].
The defilements have been burnt away by me.
Welcome indeed has come to me!
... [as before] ... the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
The four analytical knowledges (paṭisambhidā) have been attained.
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the Venerable Akkamanadāyaka Thera speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Akkamanadāyaka is the fifth.
